claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The splashdown occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The splashdown occurred at approximately 5:07 p.m. PT (8:07 p.m. ET).
The Artemis II crew concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
Recovery teams from the U.S. Navy and NASA aided the Artemis II crew.
The Artemis II mission goal was final testing of systems with crew before future lunar landings.
Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen were recovered by the U.S.S. John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II Orion capsule hit speeds over 32 times the speed of sound during reentry.
The Artemis II Orion capsule reached temperatures of nearly 5,000°F during reentry.
According to Florida Today's coverage, the Artemis II splashdown was visible as a bright streak off the coast of San Diego.
The NBC News live blog documented the successful end of the Artemis II mission.
According to UC San Diego Today, San Diego was selected due to its proximity to Pacific landing sites.
According to UC San Diego Today, the strong presence of U.S. Navy facilities in San Diego is essential for recovery operations and transporting the capsule to Naval Base San Diego.
The official NASA Instagram shared a post about the successful Artemis II mission.
Navy divers in inflatable boats surrounded the Artemis II Orion capsule, checking it for safety before the crew exited.
The Artemis II astronauts were brought out on an inflatable "front porch" and lifted by helicopter to the recovery ship.
The U.S.S. John P. Murtha’s well deck was used to store the Orion capsule for transport.
The Artemis II crew and capsule will be transported to Johnson Space Center in Houston after initial medical evaluations.
